item.title: 489: Destination Linux 489: PHP2Shell Emergency & Inside the OOSC Conference
item.author: comments@destinationlinux.net (Deviant Airwaves)
item.itunes:author: Deviant Airwaves
item.itunes:subtitle: DL 489 is packed! Ryan and Jill break down the critical PHP2Shell vulnerability, share community feedback on AI art, and sit down with Akarshan and Till from the Opportunity Open Source Conference - who used Destination Linux streaming as part of their event framework! A tight, focused episode full of open‑source insight and important security news.
item.description:
In Destination Linux Episode 489, Ryan and Jill deliver a tight, focused episode centered around community perspectives, major security news, and an inspiring interview with the organizers of India’s rapidly growing Opportunity Open Source Conference (OOSC).

We begin with community feedback on AI art, exploring how prompting, creativity, and human intention intersect in this evolving medium.

Then we dive into the PHP2Shell emergency: two critical vulnerabilities (CVE‑2026‑109618 and CVE‑2026‑109619) affecting PHP’s session.upload_progress feature. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution and forced an emergency patch release. We break down what happened, who’s affected, and what everyday users, site owners, and administrators need to do right now.

In our feature interview, we welcome Akarshan and Till Kamppeter from OOSC, founded by OpenPrinting’s Till Kamppeter and Aveek Basu. OOSC 4.0 brought together more than 500 developers, researchers, and students, and the team used Destination Linux as a framework for their streaming and event structure. We talk inspiration, challenges, community impact, and the future of OOSC.

Plus new patrons, merch shoutouts, and plenty of laughs along the way.

Boot up your favorite distro, fire up your terminal, and join us for another Linux adventure.

item.title: 488: Epic Games on Linux?! Lutris Mathieu Comandon Explores This Huge Gaming News, Steam Frame Review & F‑Droid 2.0 | DL488
item.author: comments@destinationlinux.net (Deviant Airwaves)
item.itunes:author: Deviant Airwaves
item.itunes:subtitle: Mathieu Comandon, creator of Lutris, joins Jill and Zeb with massive Linux gaming news: Epic Games Launcher Beta for Linux, EAC Linux v2, and a hands‑on look at the Steam Frame. We also cover Linus Torvalds using AI for kernel patches, Discord’s latest breach, Denmark’s “123456” password disaster, and the huge F‑Droid 2.0 overhaul. A fun, fast‑moving episode packed with Linux goodness!
item.description:
In Destination Linux Episode 488, Jill hosts an action‑packed Linux adventure with Zeb and special guest host Mathieu Comandon, creator of Lutris. Mathieu brings massive Linux gaming updates, including Easy Anti‑Cheat Linux v2, the Epic Games Launcher AppImage Beta, and his early impressions of the Steam Frame - marking one of the biggest Linux gaming leaps in years.

Jill announces upcoming Destination Linux community game streams, featuring Jackbox, Golf With Your Friends, Serious Sam, and more - all streamed on Twitch and the platform with the big red button.

Zeb covers three major news stories shaking the tech world:

  • Linus Torvalds using AI/LLMs to decipher complex kernel patches

  • A Discord data breach affecting millions

  • Denmark’s unbelievable “123456” password incident exposing 88 million records

Jill wraps up with a deep dive into F‑Droid 2.0, the largest overhaul of the privacy‑centric Android app store in nearly a decade - featuring a modern UI, expanded search, automatic background updates, and Jetpack Compose redesign.

Plus, we highlight new Patrons, community feedback, and plenty of laughs along the way.

item.description:
Welcome To Destination Linux Episode 01 – 12-17-16

This is the 1st episode of a weekly podcast/vidcast with Hosts Rob and Rocco discussing everyday Linux things.

Distro Challenge Discussion

Rob has ran KDE Neon for the last week while Rocco has run Antergos Gnome. The Distro challenge was cut short due to time during the Holidays

News

Linux Kernel 4.9 release

Linux Kernel 4.10 Features

Cub Linux Has Ceased Development

The Brisk menu will be ported over to Mate

App Pick of the Week

No App this week Distro Update

Distrowatch

Korora 25

MX16

Sudo Reboot’s Video

English Bob’s Video

Don’t Call Me Lenny

Distro Discussion

Linux Mint 18.1

Youtube Comments

Going back to the Distro challenge for a moment Brave Hippo Commented that I should check out ApricityOS. So we want your comments on which direction Rocco should go in and what specific distro you recommend for his next install. Matt also teased about having a great Distro challenge
